bias: Short-term neutral-to-bearish below $3,665 and especially $3,750–$3,800; Friday's rebound is not yet a confirmed trend reversal
confidence: Qualitative · moderate-low. A strong relief bounce conflicts with a still-hawkish rates/dollar backdrop, ETF outflows and reduced speculative longs. Market closed; no intraday signal.
bottom_line: Gold rebounded sharply on Friday from Wednesday's 15-month low of $3,426.35, but Reuters' analyst read is that the move looks more like short-covering/profit-taking than a confirmed trend change. Last accessible spot reference was $3,639.61 at 19:01 UTC on 27 Nov. Base case for the next open: test whether $3,600–$3,620 holds; failure risks $3,550–$3,565 and then $3,426.35. Bulls need to reclaim Friday's reported $3,665 area and then clear the $3,750–$3,800 seller zone. Strong dollar, 4.94% 10-year nominal yield and a fully priced December Fed hike remain headwinds. Market closed Saturday; do not treat this as a live entry signal.

drivers.name: US inflation / Federal Reserve
drivers.detail: Reuters reported that October PCE inflation rose 0.3% month-on-month after 0.5% in September. By 25 Nov, markets had fully priced a December Fed rate hike. Higher expected rates increase the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding gold.

drivers.name: US dollar and Treasury yields
drivers.detail: ICE-sourced DXY data show 104.01 at the 27 Nov close, +0.33% on the day and +2.09% from end-October; Reuters described the dollar as near a 22-month high. The official US Treasury 10-year par yield was 4.94% on 27 Nov, up from 4.85% on 25 Nov. Latest FRED 10-year TIPS real yield available at this review was 2.79% on 24 Nov; no 27 Nov real-yield observation was yet visible.
drivers.published: Daily market data through 2026-11-27; real-yield observation through 2026-11-24

drivers.name: Friday's rebound
drivers.detail: Reuters attributed the recovery to bargain-buying after the 15-month low and quoted Zain Vawda describing it as short-covering/profit-taking rather than a trend reversal. WSJ linked Friday's metals rally to renewed AI-equity risk appetite and less liquidity-driven selling. Reuters also noted improving jewellery/investment demand in India and firm Chinese retail premiums.

drivers.name: Silver / precious-metals confirmation
drivers.detail: Reuters reported spot silver up 4.7% to $43.44/oz on Friday. WSJ reported its front-month silver futures benchmark up 7.8% to $43.167; these are different quote types/timestamps and should not be conflated.

drivers.name: Speculative positioning and ETF flows
drivers.detail: CFTC data as of 17 Nov show COMEX managed-money net longs down 9,399 contracts week-on-week and legacy non-commercial net longs down 23,975. WGC weekly data reported net ETF outflows of about $2.15bn and holdings down 20.4t in the week to 20 Nov. These are delayed weekly observations, not live flow or whale order flow.
drivers.published: CFTC positions 2026-11-17; WGC weekly flow report published 2026-11-23

drivers.name: Official-sector demand
drivers.detail: World Gold Council Q3 data show central banks added 321t in the quarter, up 42% year-on-year, and year-to-date purchases reached 675t. October physically backed gold ETFs added $2.7bn and 19t to a record 4,275t, but the later week to 20 Nov saw material outflows. Structural demand therefore supports the longer horizon but does not remove near-term liquidation risk.

paths.invalidation: Sustained acceptance above $3,800 would invalidate the near-term stall case.

paths.name: Bear continuation
paths.trigger: A clean break and hold below $3,600, followed by failure to reclaim $3,550–$3,565.
paths.target: $3,550–$3,565 first, then the Reuters-reported $3,426.35 swing low. No lower target is published here without a verified support reference.
paths.invalidation: Reclaim $3,665 and then sustain above the $3,750–$3,800 seller zone.

paths.name: Bullish recovery
paths.trigger: Hold $3,600–$3,620, reclaim the $3,665 Friday high and then accept above $3,750–$3,800.
paths.target: $3,665 first, then $3,750–$3,800. Beyond that, no independently verified short-term target was found in this review; Goldman Sachs' $4,150 is a year-end forecast, not an immediate chart target.
paths.invalidation: Lose $3,600 and then fail to recover $3,550–$3,565.

professional_views.source: Reuters · Zain Vawda, market analyst at Audacity Capital
professional_views.view: Called the rebound more like short-covering/profit-taking than a trend change. Said rallies toward $3,750–$3,800 could attract sellers while real yields and the dollar remain high. A move toward $4,500 by mid-2027 would require the Fed to stop hiking and the dollar to weaken.

professional_views.source: Reuters · David Meger, director of metals trading at High Ridge Futures
professional_views.view: On 25 Nov, said the October PCE report did not ease inflation concerns and that the likelihood of further Fed rate increases remained a headwind for non-yielding gold. Reuters reported markets had fully priced a December hike.

professional_views.source: Goldman Sachs strategists · reported by Investing.com
professional_views.view: The bank cut its end-2026 gold forecast to $4,150/oz from $4,650 and end-2027 to $4,800 from $5,400, citing a hawkish Fed and normalising hedge demand, while retaining a constructive longer-term case tied to central-bank purchases.

Offered a market explanation rather than a price target: renewed enthusiasm for AI equities and a rebound in global stocks eased liquidity-driven selling and helped precious metals rally on Friday. The article also notes that higher expected Fed rates remain a counterweight.

professional_views.source: World Gold Council · Q3 Gold Demand Trends
professional_views.view: Official-sector demand remains a structural support: central banks bought 321t in Q3, +42% year-on-year; year-to-date purchases reached 675t. This is demand evidence, not a short-term price forecast.

horizon_outlook.view: Saturday 28 Nov is a closed-market day. Friday's final accessible spot reference was $3,639.61; wait for the Sunday reopen and new session data before judging momentum or liquidity.
horizon_outlook.trigger: On reopen, observe acceptance/rejection around $3,600–$3,620 and $3,665; do not infer a setup from the weekend quote.
horizon_outlook.target: No intraday target while closed. Conditional references: $3,600–$3,620 support and $3,665 first resistance.
horizon_outlook.invalidation: Any fresh Sunday gap or new macro headline can reset the levels; Friday's levels are not executable quotes.

horizon_outlook.view: The sharp rebound from $3,426.35 is real, but Reuters' analyst describes it as short-covering rather than a trend change. A strong dollar, high nominal/real yields and reduced speculative longs argue against chasing the bounce.
horizon_outlook.trigger: Hold $3,600–$3,620 and reclaim $3,665 for continuation; break and hold below $3,600 for renewed downside.
horizon_outlook.invalidation: Sustained acceptance above $3,800 weakens the near-term bearish case; loss of $3,426.35 invalidates the current recovery structure.

horizon_outlook.view: Fed tightening expectations and a firm dollar remain headwinds. Weekly ETF withdrawals and COT long reduction show investor de-risking, while central-bank demand and improving Asian physical buying are counterweights.
horizon_outlook.trigger: A sustained break above $3,800 plus softer DXY/real yields would improve the recovery case; fresh inflation strength and a break below $3,426.35 would reinforce downside.
horizon_outlook.target: No calibrated multi-week target. Goldman Sachs' $4,150 is a dated end-2026 forecast, not a near-term technical objective.
horizon_outlook.invalidation: A clear easing in the Fed path and a durable decline in real yields would challenge the bearish correction thesis.

horizon_outlook.view: Goldman Sachs retained a higher long-horizon path ($4,150 end-2026; $4,800 end-2027) after cutting both targets, and World Gold Council data show strong Q3 central-bank demand. These supports compete with persistent inflation and a higher-for-longer rate risk.
horizon_outlook.trigger: Sustained official-sector buying, ETF inflows returning and easing real yields would support the bullish structural case.
horizon_outlook.target: Published bank reference: $4,150 end-2026 and $4,800 end-2027 from Goldman Sachs' 6 Nov revision; analyst forecast only, not a model-derived destination.
horizon_outlook.invalidation: Persistently rising real yields/dollar, continued ETF redemptions and a sustained structural break below major swing support would challenge the long-term constructive view.
